themes_detail.label: Street Signs Falling Apart
themes_detail.summary: Dangling street signs spiked to 7 complaints THIS WEEK, up 2700% from the 0.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 15.59), suggesting a sudden infrastructure failure or storm damage requiring urgent public safety investigation.
evidence: 7 dangling street sign complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average (2700% spike, z-score: 15.59)
Highest z-score among all spikes, indicating most anomalous deviation from baseline
No context provided suggests potential weather event or systemic maintenance failure
reporting_angles: Canvas Crown Heights / Prospect Heights to identify clusters of dangling signs and document safety risks (e.g., pedestrian injuries, visibility hazards)
Contact NYPD and DOT to determine root cause: storm damage, deferred maintenance, or contractor negligence

themes_detail.label: Street Condition Deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Street condition complaints jumped to 22 THIS WEEK, up 309% from the 5.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.41), signaling rapid pavement or pothole damage that may correlate with recent weather or delayed repairs.
evidence: 22 street condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.4 weekly average (309% spike, z-score: 6.41)
Second-most anomalous spike this week after dangling street signs
Correlates with ongoing snow/ice complaints (743 total over 90 days) suggesting winter weather stress
reporting_angles: Map the 22 complaints geographically to identify if damage is concentrated on major thoroughfares or residential blocks
Interview DOT about repair timelines and budget constraints; compare Crown Heights repair speed to other NYC districts

themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints surged to 14 LAST WEEK, up 331% from the 3.2 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.89), potentially indicating widespread heating system failures, mold, or ventilation hazards affecting residents' homes and health.
evidence: 14 indoor air quality complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.2 weekly average (331% spike, z-score: 6.89)
Heat/hot water also top complaint category (3860 total over 90 days), suggesting heating system failures may be driving air quality issues
Timing (late March, early spring) atypical for heating complaints—may indicate late-season system breakdown or mold emergence
reporting_angles: Interview affected residents about specific symptoms (respiratory, mold odors, cold drafts) to determine if complaints share common causes
Contact NYC Department of Health to assess whether spike correlates with known heating violations or mold outbreaks in the district

themes_detail.label: Rodent Infestation Surge
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints jumped to 23 LAST WEEK, up 167% from the 8.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.25), a sustained increase that aligns with the community board's repeated requests for enhanced cleaning—suggesting systemic sanitation failures.
evidence: 23 rodent complaints LAST WEEK vs. 8.6 weekly average (167% spike, z-score: 5.25)
Community board has filed recurring budget requests for 'Other cleaning requests' (Department of Sanitation), indicating ongoing sanitation inadequacy
Gothamist article (2026-03-17) on failed enforcement against dog waste suggests broader sanitation enforcement and cleanup failures
reporting_angles: Investigate whether the 23 rodent complaints cluster in specific buildings or blocks; interview residents on trash management and Sanitation responsiveness
Analyze Sanitation's response times and fines issued for inadequate trash containment in Crown Heights vs. citywide average

themes_detail.label: Street Sweeping Neglect
themes_detail.summary: Street sweeping complaints reached 6 LAST WEEK, up 860% from the 0.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 7.72), mirroring the community board's persistent budget requests for enhanced cleaning and suggesting Sanitation is not meeting baseline maintenance standards.
evidence: 6 street sweeping complaints LAST WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average (860% spike, z-score: 7.72)
Community board's recurring budget request for 'Other cleaning requests' (Department of Sanitation) indicates this is a chronic district issue
Converges with rodent spike (23 complaints last week) and litter basket complaints (4 complaints 3 weeks ago, up 1500%), forming a sanitation failure cluster
reporting_angles: Request Sanitation's Crown Heights schedule and staffing levels; compare to pre-pandemic baseline and other high-density districts
Interview residents and local business owners on visible litter accumulation and its impact on neighborhood perception and foot traffic
